articles.title: Tech scare trade hits Nasdaq futures while crypto reels from its biggest-ever hack
articles.summary: A double miss on both EPS and revenue overshadowed the fastest growth for AWS in five years. - The executive view: Intel CFO David Zisner said "we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year." - The backdrop: Intel's stock has been on an upward tear, up about 150% so far this year prior to the earnings report, although it's down roughly 23% in October over growing concern over the size of the artificial intelligence buildout.

articles.title: Chevron beats earnings expectations as refining profits soar on high diesel fuel prices
articles.summary: Chevron shares are up about 2% in premarket trading. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. $61.6 billion expected Profits from Chevron's oil and gas production rose about 70% to $5.7 billion compared to $3.3 billion in the year-ago period.

articles.title: Amazon falls 7%, Intel plunges 25% in premarket trading, as pressure mounts after earnings
articles.summary: Amazon and Intel shares were down in premarket trading on Friday after they reported September quarter numbers that disappointed investors, dragging Nasdaq futures down 2% and capping off a week of rough tech earnings. Chip stocks including Micron, Nvidia and Arm were lower in premarket trade in the U.S., while major European semiconductor names, including ASML, saw sharp declines. Investors are nervous about the massive AI spending from the tech giants and whether that will pay off.

articles.title: BP’s third-quarter profit nearly quadruples to $8.5 billion as refining margins surge
articles.summary: Oil major BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple year-on-year. "These are dynamic times with volatility and disruption to trade flows continuing to define energy markets," BP CEO Meg O'Neill said in a statement.

articles.title: Indian AI infrastructure firm reportedly seeks to raise $3 billion of debt to buy Nvidia's next-generation chips
articles.summary: An artificial intelligence infrastructure firm in India is reportedly seeking to raise debt to fund the purchase of Nvidia's Rubin graphics processing units. AM Intelligence, a Hyderabad-based company, is planning to raise up to $3 billion through bond issues and bank loans to purchase Nvidia Corp's next-generation chips, Bloomberg reported on Friday.

articles.title: Iran claims four tankers struck mines in Hormuz as strike fears grow after U.S. midterms
articles.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported a small boat attaching two explosive devices to a tanker about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. The vital waterway carried about one-fifth of the world's energy supplies, and has seen traffic plummet to single-digit daily passings since the war started in late February.

articles.title: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013
articles.summary: The Bank of Japan declared that underlying inflation in the country was "generally consistent" with its target of 2%, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013. Before this, the BOJ used to say that underlying inflation has been "approaching 2 percent." This comes as the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
articles.summary: "Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, funding for working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt," according to a statement. Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint.

articles.title: FedEx Freight delivers a much-needed quarterly beat. Where we stand on shares now
articles.summary: Bottom line Shares rose about 3% in extended trading, a welcome market reaction considering how badly the stock has struggled. Anytime a stock is spun off, there can be an adjustment period as investors who received shares due to ownership in its former parent decide to dump it. Plus, elevated fuel prices have weighed on stocks across the transportation industry, complicating matters for FDXF shares.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is punishing the wrong tech stocks
articles.summary: Stocks fell Thursday, snapping a three-day winning streak as investors digested a fresh wave of corporate earnings. Cramer argued that investors are too quick to sell stocks alongside peers that are disappointing, overlooking key differences between businesses and creating potential buying opportunities.

articles.title: Coinbase net income surges 66% in third quarter, benefiting from bitcoin investment gains
articles.summary: Net income at the San Francisco-based platform surged thanks to the value of its volatile cryptocurrency investment portfolio, which can swing wildly even when the composition of the underlying holdings are little changed. The third quarter value of Coinbase's crypto investment portfolio climbed due to a resurgence in the digital asset market.

articles.title: Amazon AWS posts 39% revenue growth as cloud rivals also accelerate
articles.summary: Amazon's cloud-computing unit reported more rapid third-quarter growth than analysts had projected. Growth in the second quarter came in at about 37%. The AWS growth rate was the highest since the fourth quarter of 2021.

articles.title: Amazon posts negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, holds 2026 capex unchanged
articles.summary: Amazon shares plunged more than 7% in extended trading Thursday after the company reported earnings and revenue for the third quarter that fell short of Wall Street's expectations. Tech's hyperscalers have been on a blistering spending run to meet the surge in demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, but signs have begun to emerge that the capex splurge is moderating.

articles.title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.summary: The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released. A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic.

articles.title: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
articles.summary: Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead the company to profitability. $1.99 billion expected Shares of Rivian were up roughly 5% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day.

articles.title: Norwegian shares surge 13% on earnings beat, guidance raise
articles.summary: Shares of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings surged 13% Thursday after the company posted better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its outlook for the full year. The cruise line reported third-quarter revenue of $2.95 billion, topping Wall Street expectations of $2.88 billion, according to analyst estimates from LSEG. Net income for the period was $491 million, or $1.07 per share.

articles.title: Aon CEO warns AI data center insurance risks could threaten financing
articles.summary: The race to build artificial intelligence infrastructure is creating enormous new risks that could threaten financing for the data centers powering the artificial intelligence boom, according to Aon CEO Greg Case. The warnings come as technology companies accelerate spending on data centers, electricity generation and other infrastructure needed to support AI.

articles.title: ServiceNow shares plunge 27% to worst day ever after earnings revive AI disruption fears
articles.summary: ServiceNow shares sank 27% on Thursday and recorded their worst day on record after the enterprise software company's third-quarter results underwhelmed, reigniting artificial intelligence disruption concerns. The results did little to overturn recent "SaaSpocalypse" fears, or concerns that new AI capabilities will upend traditional software business models.

articles.title: Jim Cramer: Why investors are punishing Alphabet and giving Microsoft a pass
articles.summary: For Jim, the key differentiator is Microsoft's ability to keep spending in check while pursuing its artificial intelligence ambitions and delivering strong growth. The company also saw a sequential deceleration in Google Search revenue growth, fueling concerns about AI disruption for its longtime cash cow. Microsoft shares had fallen more than 25% in the first six months of the year amid concerns that the company could be left behind in the AI race.

articles.title: Big Oil earnings are set to surge. Why investors may want to be cautious
articles.summary: I'll also be meeting privately with some of the biggest power players in energy and having great conversations with country and company leaders about oil, gas, commodities, Hormuz, and more - all ahead of what some fear may be another round of hits on Iran or Iranian energy infrastructure. The next few days are critical for energy investors.

Across 19 midterm cycles from 1950 through 2022, economic growth accelerated in nine cycles, slowed in nine and remained the same in one, according to an Oct.
